question: Which statement best defines strong (linearizable) consistency?
options: Every read eventually returns the latest write if you wait long enough
Reads always reflect the most recent completed write as if operations happened instantaneously in a single global order
Reads within one session are consistent but other sessions may differ
Writes are ordered per key but reads may be stale across keys
explanation: Linearizability guarantees that once a write completes, all subsequent reads see it, and all operations appear to take effect at a single instant in a total real-time order. It is the strongest single-object guarantee.

question: Under eventual consistency, what guarantee is actually provided?
options: All replicas always return identical values immediately after a write
Reads never return stale data
If no new writes occur, all replicas eventually converge to the same value
Writes are rejected until all replicas acknowledge
explanation: Eventual consistency only promises convergence in the absence of new updates; during propagation, different replicas may return different (stale) values. It says nothing about how long convergence takes.

question: A user posts a comment and immediately refreshes the page but does not see their own comment. Which consistency model would have prevented this specific anomaly?
options: Read-your-writes (session) consistency
Monotonic reads only
Causal consistency across all users
Eventual consistency with anti-entropy
explanation: Read-your-writes guarantees a client always sees the effects of its own prior writes. This directly fixes the 'I posted but can't see it' problem, even if other users see it later.

question: In a quorum-replicated system with N replicas, which condition guarantees that a read always observes the latest committed write?
options: R + W < N
R = 1 and W = 1
W = 1 and R = N
R + W > N
explanation: When the read quorum plus the write quorum exceed the replica count (R + W > N), the read and write sets overlap by at least one replica, so a read is guaranteed to touch a node holding the newest write.

question: Causal consistency guarantees which of the following?
options: A total global order of all operations across the system
Operations that are causally related are seen by all nodes in the same order, while concurrent operations may be seen in different orders
Every replica is byte-for-byte identical at all times
Only the most recent write per key is ever visible
explanation: Causal consistency preserves the happens-before relationship: if A causally precedes B, everyone observes A before B. Concurrent (unrelated) operations have no ordering requirement, making it weaker than linearizability but stronger than eventual.
